question.text: On a road divided by a barrier, who must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights?

answer.text: On a road divided by a barrier, oncoming vehicles need not stop for a school bus with flashing red lights, but vehicles on the bus's side of the road must stop.

teaching.text: On a barrier-divided road, traffic on the bus's side stops, while oncoming traffic across the barrier need not. Remember: bus side stops, median side goes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a road divided by a barrier, oncoming vehicles need not stop for a school bus with flashing red lights, but vehicles on the bus's side of the road must stop.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: bus side stops, median side goes

question.text: What do flashing yellow hazard lights on a school bus mean?

answer.text: Flashing yellow hazard lights on a school bus mean proceed with caution.

teaching.text: Flashing yellow hazard lights on a bus mean proceed with caution. Remember: hazards mean caution.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Flashing yellow hazard lights on a school bus mean proceed with caution.

question.text: What do flashing yellow overhead lights on a school bus mean?

answer.text: Flashing yellow overhead lights on a school bus mean get ready to stop.

teaching.text: Flashing yellow overhead lights warn that the bus is about to stop, so get ready to stop. Remember: yellow overhead, get ready.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Flashing yellow overhead lights on a school bus mean get ready to stop.

question.text: What must you do when a school bus shows flashing red overhead lights?

answer.text: Flashing red overhead lights mean stop at least twenty feet from the bus and stay stopped until the red lights turn off or the bus moves on.

teaching.text: Flashing red overhead lights mean stop at least twenty feet back and stay until they go off or the bus moves. Remember: red overhead, stop and stay.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Flashing red overhead lights mean stop at least twenty feet from the bus and stay stopped until the red lights turn off or the bus moves on.

question.text: How do the three school bus light signals differ?

answer.text: Yellow hazard lights on a bus mean caution, yellow overhead lights mean prepare to stop, and only red overhead lights require you to stop twenty feet back.

teaching.text: Hazard lights mean caution, yellow overhead lights mean get ready, and red overhead lights mean stop twenty feet back. Remember: caution, ready, stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Yellow hazard lights on a bus mean caution, yellow overhead lights mean prepare to stop, and only red overhead lights require you to stop twenty feet back.

question.text: Must you yield when turning right, including on a red light?

answer.text: You must yield to other vehicles when turning right, including a right turn at a red light.

teaching.text: Turning right, even on red, means yielding to other vehicles. Remember: right turns yield.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You must yield to other vehicles when turning right, including a right turn at a red light.

question.text: When must you yield while turning left?

answer.text: You must yield to other vehicles when turning left, whether out of a driveway or alley or while finishing a left turn on a green light.

teaching.text: Turning left from a driveway, an alley or on a green light means yielding to other vehicles. Remember: left turns yield.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You must yield to other vehicles when turning left, whether out of a driveway or alley or while finishing a left turn on a green light.

question.text: Does a left turn on red require yielding?

answer.text: A left turn on a red light also requires yielding to other vehicles.

teaching.text: A left turn on red also requires yielding to other vehicles. Remember: left on red yields too.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A left turn on a red light also requires yielding to other vehicles.

question.text: What must you do before turning left on red from one one-way street onto another?

answer.text: Before turning left on red from one one-way street onto another, stop completely and look for traffic coming from your right.

teaching.text: From one one-way street onto another, stop completely and look right before a left on red. Remember: stop, look right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before turning left on red from one one-way street onto another, stop completely and look for traffic coming from your right.

question.text: What does a left on red from a two-way street onto a one-way street require?

answer.text: Turning left on red from a two-way street onto a one-way street requires a full stop, a scan to the right, and yielding to opposite vehicles turning right.

teaching.text: From a two-way street onto a one-way street, stop, scan right, and yield to opposite vehicles turning right. Remember: stop, scan right, yield.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Turning left on red from a two-way street onto a one-way street requires a full stop, a scan to the right, and yielding to opposite vehicles turning right.

question.text: When your light has just turned green, who do you yield to first?

answer.text: When your light has just turned green, yield to any vehicles still in the intersection before you go.

teaching.text: On a fresh green, let vehicles still in the intersection clear before you go. Remember: clear the intersection first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When your light has just turned green, yield to any vehicles still in the intersection before you go.

question.text: When may you turn left on a green light, and what if it turns red mid-turn?

answer.text: On a green light, turn left only after all oncoming traffic has cleared, and if the light turns red while you are in the intersection, finish the turn as quickly and safely as possible.

teaching.text: Turn left on green only after oncoming traffic clears, and finish the turn safely if the light turns red. Remember: wait for oncoming to clear.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a green light, turn left only after all oncoming traffic has cleared, and if the light turns red while you are in the intersection, finish the turn as quickly and safely as possible.

question.text: What does a green light not give you the right of way over?

answer.text: A green light does not give you the right of way over vehicles still clearing the intersection or over oncoming traffic when you turn left.

teaching.text: Green never beats vehicles still clearing the intersection or oncoming traffic on your left turn. Remember: green is not a guarantee.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A green light does not give you the right of way over vehicles still clearing the intersection or over oncoming traffic when you turn left.

question.text: How do you handle a stop sign or flashing red signal, and where do you stop?

answer.text: At a stop sign or flashing red signal, stop completely and check traffic, using the stop line or crosswalk, or else a spot where you can see approaching traffic without entering the intersection.

teaching.text: Stop completely at the stop line, the crosswalk, or a spot with a clear view, without entering the intersection. Remember: full stop, then look.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a stop sign or flashing red signal, stop completely and check traffic, using the stop line or crosswalk, or else a spot where you can see approaching traffic without entering the intersection.

question.text: Who goes first at a four-way stop, and who yields on a tie?

answer.text: At a four-way stop, the first driver to arrive and stop goes first, and when two arrive together the vehicle on the left yields to the one on its right.

teaching.text: At a four-way stop the first to stop goes first, and on a tie the left yields to the right. Remember: first stops, first goes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a four-way stop, the first driver to arrive and stop goes first, and when two arrive together the vehicle on the left yields to the one on its right.

question.text: How do you handle a malfunctioning traffic signal?

answer.text: At a malfunctioning traffic signal, stop completely, yield to vehicles already there, and yield to the vehicle on your right if you arrive together.

teaching.text: At a dark or broken signal, stop fully, let vehicles already there go, and yield to the right on a tie. Remember: dead signal, treat as stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a malfunctioning traffic signal, stop completely, yield to vehicles already there, and yield to the vehicle on your right if you arrive together.

question.text: What must you do at a flashing yellow arrow?

answer.text: At a flashing yellow arrow, yield to traffic before you complete your turn.

teaching.text: A flashing yellow arrow means yield to traffic before you finish the turn. Remember: yield, then turn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a flashing yellow arrow, yield to traffic before you complete your turn.

question.text: At a T-intersection with no signs or signals, who has the right of way?

answer.text: At a T-intersection with no signals or signs, vehicles on the through road have the right of way.

teaching.text: At a T-intersection with no signs or signals, the through road has the right of way. Remember: through road wins.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a T-intersection with no signals or signs, vehicles on the through road have the right of way.

question.text: What should you do at a YIELD sign?

answer.text: At a YIELD sign, slow down, check for traffic and be ready to stop.

teaching.text: At a YIELD sign, slow down, check for traffic and be ready to stop. Remember: slow, look, be ready.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a YIELD sign, slow down, check for traffic and be ready to stop.

question.text: At a four-way stop, when does the left driver yield to the right?

answer.text: At a four-way stop the first to stop goes first, and only on a tie does the driver on the left yield to the driver on the right.

teaching.text: The first to stop goes first; only on a tie does the left driver yield to the right. Remember: ties go right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a four-way stop the first to stop goes first, and only on a tie does the driver on the left yield to the driver on the right.

question.text: How should a malfunctioning signal be treated?

answer.text: A malfunctioning signal is treated like a stop: stop fully, let vehicles already there go, and on a tie yield to the right.

teaching.text: Treat a broken signal like a stop: stop fully, let those already there go, and yield to the right on a tie. Remember: broken signal, full stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A malfunctioning signal is treated like a stop: stop fully, let vehicles already there go, and on a tie yield to the right.

question.text: How does a flashing yellow arrow differ from a flashing red signal?

answer.text: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn but only after yielding, while a flashing red signal requires a complete stop first.

teaching.text: A flashing yellow arrow means yield then turn, while a flashing red means stop first. Remember: arrow yields, red stops.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn but only after yielding, while a flashing red signal requires a complete stop first.

question.text: At a T-intersection without signs, who yields?

answer.text: At a T-intersection without signs, the driver on the ending road yields to traffic on the through road.

teaching.text: On the road that ends at a T-intersection, you yield to the through road. Remember: ending road yields.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a T-intersection without signs, the driver on the ending road yields to traffic on the through road.

question.text: Who should you be ready to yield to in work areas and near stopped service vehicles?

answer.text: Be ready to yield to workers in construction or maintenance areas and when nearing or passing a stopped garbage, utility or road maintenance vehicle with flashing lights.

teaching.text: Be ready to yield to workers and to stopped garbage, utility or road maintenance vehicles with flashing lights. Remember: yield to workers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Be ready to yield to workers in construction or maintenance areas and when nearing or passing a stopped garbage, utility or road maintenance vehicle with flashing lights.

question.text: What should you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren?

answer.text: When an emergency vehicle approaches with red or blue lights and a siren, pull right next to the curb or edge, clear of any intersection, and stop until it passes or an officer waves you on.

teaching.text: For lights and a siren, pull right to the curb clear of intersections and stop until it passes or an officer waves you on. Remember: pull right and stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When an emergency vehicle approaches with red or blue lights and a siren, pull right next to the curb or edge, clear of any intersection, and stop until it passes or an officer waves you on.

question.text: What should you do at a MERGE sign?

answer.text: At a MERGE sign, adjust your speed and yield to through traffic so you can merge safely.

teaching.text: At a MERGE sign, adjust your speed and yield to through traffic. Remember: match speed, yield, merge.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a MERGE sign, adjust your speed and yield to through traffic so you can merge safely.

question.text: What right of way does a funeral procession have?

answer.text: A funeral procession has the right of way over all vehicles except fire trucks, ambulances and police vehicles.

teaching.text: A funeral procession outranks all vehicles except fire trucks, ambulances and police. Remember: processions yield only to responders.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A funeral procession has the right of way over all vehicles except fire trucks, ambulances and police vehicles.

question.text: What flag must funeral procession vehicles fly?

answer.text: Procession vehicles must fly a fluorescent orange flag bearing a religious symbol such as a cross, a star of David, or a crescent and star.

teaching.text: Procession vehicles fly a fluorescent orange flag with a religious symbol. Remember: orange flag, religious symbol.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Procession vehicles must fly a fluorescent orange flag bearing a religious symbol such as a cross, a star of David, or a crescent and star.

question.text: Is cutting through a funeral procession allowed, and must you pull over?

answer.text: Cutting through a funeral procession is a civil infraction, though drivers are not required to pull over when they meet one.

teaching.text: Cutting through a funeral procession is a civil infraction, though you need not pull over. Remember: never cut through.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Cutting through a funeral procession is a civil infraction, though drivers are not required to pull over when they meet one.

question.text: What must you do and not do when meeting a funeral procession?

answer.text: Funeral processions outrank all traffic except fire, ambulance and police vehicles, yet you are not required to pull over for one; you only must not cut through it.

teaching.text: Processions outrank all but fire, ambulance and police vehicles; you need not pull over, only never cut through. Remember: don't cut, no need to stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Funeral processions outrank all traffic except fire, ambulance and police vehicles, yet you are not required to pull over for one; you only must not cut through it.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: don't cut, no need to stop

question.text: Must you yield to a pedestrian in a marked crosswalk when your light is green?

answer.text: Yield to pedestrians in a marked crosswalk, whether at an intersection or midblock, even when your light is green.

teaching.text: Pedestrians in a marked crosswalk, at a corner or midblock, go first even on your green. Remember: crosswalk beats green.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Yield to pedestrians in a marked crosswalk, whether at an intersection or midblock, even when your light is green.

question.text: Which other pedestrians must you yield to?

answer.text: Yield to children in or near a school zone crosswalk while school is in session, and to pedestrians with physical, hearing or visual disabilities.

teaching.text: Yield to children near school zone crosswalks during school, and to pedestrians with disabilities. Remember: school kids, disabled walkers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Yield to children in or near a school zone crosswalk while school is in session, and to pedestrians with physical, hearing or visual disabilities.

question.text: When turning at an intersection, must you yield to pedestrians even without signals?

answer.text: Yield to pedestrians on every turn at an intersection, whether or not lights or traffic control devices are present.

teaching.text: On every turn at an intersection, with or without signals, yield to pedestrians. Remember: every turn, yield to walkers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Yield to pedestrians on every turn at an intersection, whether or not lights or traffic control devices are present.

question.text: At which stops and signals must you yield to pedestrians?

answer.text: Yield to pedestrians when stopping at a stop sign or flashing red light and at an intersection with a flashing yellow light.

teaching.text: Yield to pedestrians at stop signs, flashing red lights and flashing yellow lights. Remember: stops and flashing yellow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Yield to pedestrians when stopping at a stop sign or flashing red light and at an intersection with a flashing yellow light.

question.text: Where no traffic control devices exist, when does a pedestrian in an unmarked crosswalk get the right of way?

answer.text: Where no traffic control devices exist, a pedestrian using an unmarked crosswalk on the driver's half of the road gets the right of way.

teaching.text: With no traffic control devices, a pedestrian in an unmarked crosswalk on your half of the road goes first. Remember: your half, their right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Where no traffic control devices exist, a pedestrian using an unmarked crosswalk on the driver's half of the road gets the right of way.

question.text: Which other pedestrians must you yield to, even after the signal changes?

answer.text: Yield to a pedestrian who stepped into a crosswalk before the signal changed, and to one crossing from an alley, driveway, building or private road.

teaching.text: Yield to pedestrians who entered before the signal changed and to those crossing from alleys or driveways. Remember: already crossing, still yield.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Yield to a pedestrian who stepped into a crosswalk before the signal changed, and to one crossing from an alley, driveway, building or private road.

question.text: Does a green light override a pedestrian already in the crosswalk?

answer.text: A green light never overrides a pedestrian already in the crosswalk.

teaching.text: A pedestrian already in the crosswalk goes first, even when your light turns green. Remember: walkers before green.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A green light never overrides a pedestrian already in the crosswalk.

question.text: When may you pass on a two-lane highway?

answer.text: On a two-lane highway, pass only with a clear view of the left lane and oncoming traffic far enough away to give you the time and distance to pass safely.

teaching.text: Pass on a two-lane highway only with a clear view and oncoming traffic far enough away. Remember: clear view, enough room.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a two-lane highway, pass only with a clear view of the left lane and oncoming traffic far enough away to give you the time and distance to pass safely.

question.text: After passing, when may you move back to the right?

answer.text: After passing, do not cut back right until the whole vehicle you passed shows in your rearview mirror.

teaching.text: After passing, return right only when the whole vehicle you passed shows in your rearview mirror. Remember: see it in the mirror.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After passing, do not cut back right until the whole vehicle you passed shows in your rearview mirror.

question.text: How close to an oncoming vehicle may you be before you are back in your lane?

answer.text: You must be back in your lane before coming within two hundred feet of an oncoming vehicle.

teaching.text: Be back in your lane before you are within two hundred feet of an oncoming vehicle. Remember: back by two hundred feet.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You must be back in your lane before coming within two hundred feet of an oncoming vehicle.

question.text: What extra care applies when towing, passing several vehicles or following a passer?

answer.text: Allow extra passing room when towing a trailer, pass only one vehicle at a time, and do not tailgate a vehicle that is passing slower traffic.

teaching.text: Allow extra room when towing, pass one vehicle at a time, and never tailgate a passing vehicle. Remember: one at a time.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Allow extra passing room when towing a trailer, pass only one vehicle at a time, and do not tailgate a vehicle that is passing slower traffic.

question.text: What care is needed when passing in a three-lane road's center lane?

answer.text: Use extreme care when passing in the center lane of a three-lane road, since oncoming drivers may enter it too, and never use it to pass or merge when it is marked for left turns only.

teaching.text: Use extreme care in a three-lane center lane, and never pass or merge there when it is left-turn only. Remember: center lane, extreme care.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Use extreme care when passing in the center lane of a three-lane road, since oncoming drivers may enter it too, and never use it to pass or merge when it is marked for left turns only.

question.text: What should you do when someone is passing you?

answer.text: When someone is passing you, do not speed up or race them; let them finish safely.

teaching.text: When someone passes you, keep your speed and let them finish. Remember: never race a passer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When someone is passing you, do not speed up or race them; let them finish safely.

question.text: Is passing on the right ever allowed, and what is never allowed?

answer.text: Passing on the right is allowed in limited cases but never by driving on the shoulder or off the road.

teaching.text: Passing on the right is allowed only in limited cases, and never on the shoulder or off the road. Remember: never use the shoulder.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Passing on the right is allowed in limited cases but never by driving on the shoulder or off the road.

question.text: When may you pass on the right?

answer.text: You may pass on the right on a two-lane road with room when the vehicle ahead is turning left, on a multi-lane one-way street, on roads with two or more lanes each way, or where the road is widened for passing.

teaching.text: You may pass on the right around a left turner with room, on multi-lane roads, or where the road widens for passing. Remember: left turner or extra lanes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You may pass on the right on a two-lane road with room when the vehicle ahead is turning left, on a multi-lane one-way street, on roads with two or more lanes each way, or where the road is widened for passing.

question.text: When is passing on the right legal, and what makes it illegal?

answer.text: Passing on the right is legal in the listed cases, but using the shoulder or leaving the pavement to do it never is.

teaching.text: Right-side passing is legal in the listed cases, but never on the shoulder or off the pavement. Remember: listed cases, never shoulder.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Passing on the right is legal in the listed cases, but using the shoulder or leaving the pavement to do it never is.

question.text: When do lane markings, signs, hills or curves ban passing?

answer.text: Passing is banned when your side of the center has a solid yellow line, when no-passing signs are posted, or when a hill or curve hides oncoming traffic.

teaching.text: A solid yellow line on your side, a no-passing sign, or a hill or curve hiding traffic all ban passing. Remember: solid yellow, no pass.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Passing is banned when your side of the center has a solid yellow line, when no-passing signs are posted, or when a hill or curve hides oncoming traffic.

question.text: How close to an intersection, railroad crossing or blocking structure may you pass?

answer.text: Do not pass within one hundred feet of an intersection or railroad crossing, or when a bridge, viaduct or tunnel within one hundred feet blocks your view.

teaching.text: Never pass within one hundred feet of an intersection or railroad crossing, or near a bridge or tunnel that blocks your view. Remember: not within one hundred feet.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not pass within one hundred feet of an intersection or railroad crossing, or when a bridge, viaduct or tunnel within one hundred feet blocks your view.

question.text: What traffic, view or lane conditions ban passing?

answer.text: Do not pass when oncoming traffic is too close, when you cannot see clearly ahead, or when the three-lane center lane is marked left turn only.

teaching.text: Do not pass with oncoming traffic too close, with a poor view ahead, or in a left-turn-only center lane. Remember: too close, too blind.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not pass when oncoming traffic is too close, when you cannot see clearly ahead, or when the three-lane center lane is marked left turn only.

question.text: Which stopped vehicles and zones ban passing?

answer.text: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk or intersection for a pedestrian, in a posted no-passing construction zone, or when a school bus has stopped with red lights flashing.

teaching.text: Never pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian, in a posted no-passing work zone, or a bus stopped with flashing reds. Remember: never pass a stopped bus.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk or intersection for a pedestrian, in a posted no-passing construction zone, or when a school bus has stopped with red lights flashing.

question.text: How do the two hundred foot and one hundred foot passing distances differ?

answer.text: After passing, you must be back in your lane before you are within two hundred feet of oncoming traffic, while the no-passing distance near intersections and railroad crossings is one hundred feet.

teaching.text: Two hundred feet is the return distance from oncoming traffic; one hundred feet is the no-passing distance at crossings. Remember: two hundred back, one hundred near.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After passing, you must be back in your lane before you are within two hundred feet of oncoming traffic, while the no-passing distance near intersections and railroad crossings is one hundred feet.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: two hundred back, one hundred near

question.text: When may the three-lane center lane not be used to pass?

answer.text: The center lane of a three-lane road may be used to pass unless it is marked for left turns only, in which case passing and merging there are banned.

teaching.text: A three-lane center lane can be used to pass unless it is marked for left turns only. Remember: turn-only means no passing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The center lane of a three-lane road may be used to pass unless it is marked for left turns only, in which case passing and merging there are banned.

hooks_spoken: Hazards mean caution, yellow overhead means get ready, red overhead means stop twenty feet back.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of school bus signals. Hazards mean caution, yellow overhead means get ready, red overhead means stop twenty feet back. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of yielding on turns and green lights. Every turn yields, even on red, and a fresh green waits for the intersection to clear. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of stops, signals and intersections. First to stop goes first; on a tie, yield to the right. A dead signal is a full stop, and a T-intersection favors the through road. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Pull right and stop for sirens, yield at merges, and never cut through a procession.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of special right-of-way situations. Pull right and stop for sirens, yield at merges, and never cut through a procession. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Pedestrians in crosswalks go first, even on your green.

recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of yielding to pedestrians. Pedestrians in crosswalks go first, even on your green. Yield to walkers on every turn. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Pass only with a clear view and room, and return when the car shows in your mirror.

recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of passing safely. Pass only with a clear view and room, and return when the car shows in your mirror. Pass on the right only in listed cases, never on the shoulder. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: No passing at a solid yellow on your side, near hills or curves, or within one hundred feet of crossings.
Never pass a stopped school bus with flashing reds.
